name: Andrew Borstein
body:
Paul would be 42 today. Happy birthday, Ras. 

1. 2017 - Don & Kara's wedding. Paul and I were guests but also co-DJ/emcees. One of our last and best gigs together. We made a great team — he'd bring the absolute bangers to the dance floor and I'd try and make sure they were clean and hopefully not on the no-play list. He was such a magical mix of reliable and spontaneous.  

2. 1997 - Arnold Ave in Edgewood, outside Ian's house. Paul was my perpetual plus one in high school, and were kind of a package deal from then on. But after college I was the one tagging along, gratefully basking in the large social shadow he cast, absorbing all the good vibes he put out and the good will he engendered. 

3. 2011 - Paul taught me how to mix on his CD-Js and this was my first real set at some basement bar downtown. We shared an apartment together above the bakery for a short but memorable time when I was about 27. Some of the most fun, care free years of my entire life. We basically lived at Wild Colonial, our names always on the chalkboard for the pool table. This was the start of our mutual love for, in our parlance, "linking-and-clinking". 

4. 2015 - This was our first "press photo" for Above the Clouds Entertainment, our DJ collaborative, taken at a wedding photo booth probably in upstate NY. Early on we DJ'ed all the events together, with me mostly handling the mic (he was still developing his non-Patois voice) and helping to plan and execute the details. He was a natural at bringing the party and a rare wedding DJ that wasn't corny and genuinely loved his job — getting people hyped and dancing. 

5. 2019 - We rode this route so many times together, the same one he took on his last ride. He moved slowly, always on "Paul Time". Wake up late, take an easy ride from Edgewood to PVD, say hi to everyone, pay in cash, sit outside, enjoy your coffee. No rush, just appreciation and presence. He never wore a helmet and preferred to ride on the middle divider straddling both directions of traffic (he was certain it was more visible and so safer). He has lots of funny ideas, it was a big part of his charm. 

6. 2021 - By now we're at the end of full lockdown but still wearing masks out. Mere and I are about to leave for our RV adventure in MARV and Paul and I are having a last hurrah at our old stomping grounds. The day before we were set to leave I couldn't get our new bike rack installed into our RV hitch and Paul said we should just smash it harder. He brought a sledge hammer and we smashed the heck out of it. That turned out to be a very bad idea and we ended up begging a local mechanic to help us at 10pm that night to get it unstuck and properly sanded down. Paul was always there to help, no matter what, brimming with optimism, sincerity, and quirky perspectives. 

7. 2022 - Paul hosted my bachelor party at a rental house in VT and the thing that people still talk about to this day is how good the food was. His packing list was 90% groceries and cookware. And he made the owners bring us actual cast iron pans, which he insisted were necessary to cook a proper steak. The most memorable part of that weekend might literally be the amazing salad he made. 

8. 2022 - As the best man at my wedding, Paul took a decidedly relaxed approach to the toast. But he didn't have any other gear besides relaxed, which is honestly what’s so lovable about him. Didn't write down any notes either, just gave it some thought and then winged it. Paul's friendship came without pretense or reservation, built on unwavering kindness not by choice but by his very nature. 

9. 2023 - This was taken on Paul's recently acquired DSLR in my mom's backyard, 8 months after Winnie was born and 3 months after Oli was born. He was starting to get into photography in large part to capture his experience with fatherhood the same way his dad captured much of his childhood. He was so excited to be a dad, and for us to be dads together. Brittany said this was the only photo, printed out, on his desk. 

10. 2024 - This is the last time I saw Paul, just a few weeks before he died. Winnie and Mere and I visited RI and he hosted us for dinner. Oli was excited to share his ball pit and Bluey bubble toy with Winnie. Winnie could not get enough of being pushed around in the mini toy car by Paul. Paul was proud to be sharing N/A beers with me, 4 months sober. He had just installed a new fence in their backyard, one that would last. It was really wonderful.
title: Happy birthday, Ras.
